key_terms: A user-defined function that produces one output value per input row. In DataFusion Python, it receives whole Arrow arrays and must return an Arrow array of the declared type.
The declared stability of a function, such as immutable or volatile, which tells the optimizer whether it may constant fold or reuse the function's results.
A UDF body that applies an Arrow compute kernel to a whole array instead of running a Python loop over individual values.
How a function treats missing inputs, such as returning null when an argument is null, which must agree with the declared types and the query's meaning.

worked_examples.title: Register a vectorized scalar function
worked_examples.code:
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc
from datafusion import SessionContext, udf

ctx = SessionContext()
batch = pa.table({"id": [1, 2, 3], "meters": pa.array([1, 25, None], type=pa.int64())})
ctx.register_record_batches("distances", [batch.to_batches()])
to_cm = udf(lambda values: pc.multiply(values, 100), [pa.int64()], pa.int64(), "immutable", "cm")
ctx.register_udf(to_cm)
print(
    ctx.sql(
        "SELECT cm(meters) AS cm, meters * 100 AS native FROM distances ORDER BY id"
    ).to_pylist()
)
worked_examples.interpretation: Expect three rows where both columns read 100, 2500 and null. The function receives a whole Arrow array per batch, so the null stays null without any special handling. Marking it immutable lets the optimizer treat equal inputs as equal outputs; declaring a function immutable when it reads a clock or a random source would allow caching or folding that returns stale values.

worked_examples.title: Make a zero fill an explicit, named choice
worked_examples.code:
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc

meters = pa.array([1, 25, None], type=pa.int64())
print(pc.multiply(meters, 100).to_pylist())
print(pc.multiply(pc.fill_null(meters, 0), 100).to_pylist())
worked_examples.interpretation: The first list keeps the missing distance unknown and the second turns it into zero centimeters, which downstream sums and averages will treat as a real measurement. The lesson registers the second behavior under the name missing_as_zero so a reader of the SQL can see the choice. Hiding a fill inside a function with a neutral name is the defect to look for in review.

evidence: Complete actual local program with independent expected values and explicit negative checks; distributed-system claims are excluded.
